article.headline: WikWok Turns Wikipedia Into a TikTok-Style Feed
article.lede: A developer named Surya Dantuluri built WikWok, a clone of TikTok's interface that serves short, looping educational animations sourced from Wikipedia. The feed algorithm is recursively improved by a large language model (LLM) with a live coding environment, making the recommendation system self-updating in real time.
article.body:
WikWok reimagines short-form video as a canvas for educational content. Each video is a looped animation drawn from a Wikipedia article, and the 'For You' feed is powered by an LLM that continuously rewrites its own ranking algorithm. The system uses Cloudflare Durable Objects to keep state synchronized across all users globally, tracking views, likes, bookmarks, and chats in real time.

The project builds on an earlier experiment called Sudo, which generated user interfaces on the fly. By giving the LLM a REPL (a live programming environment), WikWok lets the model tweak the feed logic based on engagement signals — a form of recursive self-improvement. This is a novel approach: most recommendation systems are tuned offline by engineers, not by the model itself during runtime.

While the idea is clever, it's worth noting that TikTok's actual algorithm relies on a vast array of signals — watch time, likes, shares, comments, rewatches, skips, hashtags, and even music — processed through a sophisticated neural network. WikWok's approach is far simpler and may not scale to the same level of personalization. Still, as a proof of concept, it demonstrates how LLMs can be used to build adaptive, self-modifying systems.

The project has attracted over 180,000 views on its landing page, suggesting strong interest in AI-driven, educational short-form content. It also raises questions about content moderation and quality control when the algorithm is effectively writing its own rules.

concepts.definition: A recommendation system that uses a language model to continuously rewrite its own ranking logic based on real-time user engagement data. Instead of engineers manually updating the algorithm, the model itself modifies the code that determines which videos appear in a user's feed.

A serverless computing primitive from Cloudflare that provides a single, consistent state for a given entity (like a user or a room) across all requests. They enable real-time, globally synchronized updates without the complexity of traditional databases.

Short for Read-Eval-Print Loop, an interactive programming environment that takes single user inputs, executes them, and returns the result. In WikWok, the LLM uses a REPL to test and deploy new feed-ranking code on the fly.

repos.summary: A Next.js app that clones TikTok's UI to display short educational animations sourced from Wikipedia. Its feed algorithm is recursively updated by an LLM with a REPL, and it uses Durable Objects for real-time global state synchronization.
